title: Calibrating the thermometer
caption: The thermometer reads 1.5 °C at the ice point and 98 °C at the steam point, so true temperatures are spread over 96.5 instead of 100 scale divisions: a scale factor of 100/(98 − 1.5) = 1.0363. A reading of 50 °C therefore means a true 50.3 °C.
alt: Straight line of true temperature against thermometer reading through (1.5, 0) and (98.0, 100); a reading of 50.0 degrees corresponds to a true 50.3 degrees.
description: Horizontal axis: what the thermometer reads; vertical axis: the true temperature, both in °C.
Two fixed points anchor the calibration line: reading 1.5 ↔ true 0 °C (melting ice) and reading 98 ↔ true 100 °C (boiling water).
The slope is 1.0363, so true T = (reading − 1.5) × 1.0363.
At a reading of 50 °C the line gives 50.3 °C, about 0.3 °C above the reading.
